issue_context.title: Update TaskFlow API example to use `@dag` decorator
issue_context.body:
**Description**

Update https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/master/airflow/example_dags/tutorial_taskflow_api_etl.py tp use `@dag` decorator instead of leveraging context manager to make it more TaskFlow-y.
comments:
Do we need other example than this one?
https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/0cd1c846b2fb4d830b87e11b884094ee4765ab22/airflow/example_dags/example_dag_decorator.py#L43-L67
I was thinking more on having a more end to end example for the tutorial?
We could update an example in https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/12170 to use the `dag` decorator
Is this what you had in mind?

@kaxil I would encourage all TaskFlow tutorials to be using `@dag` better? We can leave some w context manager so people undertstand it's usable in both ways. But I was indeed refering to `tutorial_taskflow_api_etl` as @eflann mentions
Hey @casassg  @turbaszek -> is it something we want for 2.0.0rc1 ? Or if not - can yo please move the milestone to 2.1.
This is documentation update. I would think it can be even done after release of 2.0 (aka 2.0.1?)

review_comments: We'll need to see how this renders in context -- we may need to make it clearer what this does

Documentation in `@dag` decorator should  be a function `__doc__`
```suggestion
def tutorial_taskflow_api_etl():
  """### TaskFlow API Tutorial Documentation
  This is a simple ETL data pipeline example which demonstrates the use of the TaskFlow API
  using three simple tasks for Extract, Transform, and Load.
  Documentation that goes along with the Airflow TaskFlow API tutorial located
  [here](https://airflow.apache.org/docs/stable/tutorial_taskflow_api.html)
  """
```
